content: For individuals diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, certain non-insulin injectable medications, such as pramlintide and GLP-1 receptor agonists, can play a role in supporting glycemic control. Pramlintide, which has been approved specifically for use in type 1 diabetes, provides modest reductions in hemoglobin A1C levels and body weight. However, it is important to note that pramlintide is not a replacement for insulin therapy. On the other hand, GLP-1 receptor agonists, while only approved for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, have demonstrated some benefits in individuals with type 1 diabetes. These benefits include modest improvements in weight management, reductions in insulin dosage requirements, and slight decreases in A1C levels.
